newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, upward trend to continue.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, upward trend to continue.

text.p: Croatian stocks rose on a low turnover on Thursday, with new gains among hotel stocks, and traders said they expected the upward trend to continue at least for a while.
"I would not be surprised if the Istrian hoteliers rose by 20 percent in the next few days," said a trader at Metroholding brokerage.

"But I would struggle to provide an economic analysis to support that expectation -- share prices are on the rise because of speculations about foreign investment rather than for sound economic reasons."
He said the small number of shares on offer is the main reason for growth.
* Of 11 active issues eight were up, one fell and two remained flat.
* Most actively traded hotelier Suncani Hvar edged up one kuna to close at 45, on volume of 11,715 shares.
* Fully listed Zagrebacka Banka edged up five kuna to 1,010 on a modest volume of 72 shares.
* Another blue chip drugs firm Pliva traded flat at 13,000 throughout the session with 19 shares changing hands.
*The biggest gains were recorded by Istrian hoteliers:
- Laguna climbed 70 kuna to 1,000 on volume of 87 shares.
- Arenaturist jumped 45 kuna to 195, trading 300 shares.
- Riviera up 40 kuna to close at 205, with 335 shares sold
- Jadranturist inched up five kuna to 375, with only three shares sold.
* Insurer Croatia Osiguranje gained three kuna to 950, trading 169 shares for the first time since May.
* Food processor Podravka edged up 0.5 kuna to 274.5 kuna selling 1,536 shares.
* The only loser was cable-maker Elka, going down one kuna to 190, on a meagre volume of three shares.
* Confectioner Kras remained flat at 620, trading 1,271 units.
* Daily share volume up at 15,595, total turnover lower at 2.2 million kuna.
* Central bank's exchange rate: 5.4293 kuna = $1. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
